findings.text: the head gate log the manifest's after_suite names carries no header at all - its first line is 'bringing up nodes...' and its last is '240 passed in 202.80s (0:03:22)' - so the log's own bytes state no revision, tree or command, and the only carrier of that identity is the manifest's after_suite JSON. The prior review's receipt finding was that this log named the wrong revision; it is answered by removing the label rather than by correcting it, so a reader who opens the named log cannot tie these bytes to 3005ac1a or to any tree. gate-base.log in the same directory does carry revision, worktree and command header lines ('# revision: 658ba243 (dispatch base source; head tests)  tree: 22f17d32...'), so the contract is understood and unmet on one side only.

the final manifest writes baseline_suite as prose, not the armed-only JSON shape the manifest contract defines, so the base receipt is unreachable to the store's reader: _gate_log_path returns the sentence as a bare path, _read_gate_log opens nothing, and annotate_review_of_run stores added_failure_count None with the note 'unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken' - measured against the real run through the reader. gate-base.log exists in the same run directory with a header of its own and '8 failed, 249 passed in 225.55s', EXIT=1, so the base arm ran and its receipt is on disk; the record left behind just cannot be read back. The manifest's own claim - 'the head gate is green (0 failures), so the change adds zero failures by id and no base arm is needed' - is therefore asserted rather than derived by any reader, and it reads 'not run this attempt' while a base log from this same attempt sits beside it.

_worktree_repository_changes drops every untracked path whose first path part is '.venv', so a repository change confined to a path literally named .venv (or anything beneath it) is invisible to the measurement the guard rests on; measured in arm p8: an unignored .venv symlink leaves the worktree reading clean and the review promotes. The exclusion is deliberate and documented for the provisioned symlink, and a source change under .venv is not plausible, so this is a bounded blind spot rather than a route a worker can walk - recorded because the guard's sentence says the worktree shows no repository change, and in that one subtree it does not ask.

justifications.durability: the rule is held by the node's own cases, which build a real git worktree per run with the base sha recorded at dispatch - the untracked, committed-beyond-base and modified-tracked arms exercise the measurement rather than the prose, and the declared mutation reddens the committed-none case first (reproduced here: the failure is test_a_review_whose_worktree_committed_a_file_is_refused[none]). Deductions: the .venv first-part exclusion (finding 3) and the base-arm claim the store cannot re-derive (finding 2).
justifications.evidence: the head gate the manifest names records 240 passed; the base gate the run directory holds lists the node's own new cases as its only failures, all green at head, so no added failure survives by id at either revision. My own 22-arm table on both trees, the mutation arm reddening the committed-none case first, and the reader measurement stand beside it. Deductions: the head log's missing header (finding 1) and the unresolvable baseline_suite (finding 2).
justifications.fit: the change follows the module's helper-and-docstring idiom, names its helpers by mechanism (_worktree_repository_changes, _worktree_git_paths, _require_commit_for_changed_manifest), documents why no shape rule can separate a filename from a declaration, and carries conventional commit subjects with bodies and no plan, sprint or ticket label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: all five clauses of the brief are implemented and independently reproduced, and the change is strictly better in both directions - it closes a route the base left open (an untracked-only worktree change promoted under changed_paths 'none') and removes the hand edit (two prose shapes refused at the base on a clean worktree). The deduction is the base-arm receipt the record cannot read back (finding 2).
justifications.scope_discipline: the reviewed diff is exactly the five declared paths; the figure and the fragment stay inside their declared directories; the code change touches only reckon/crew/promotion.py and its two test files.
